propositions: The tickets branch is 1.04 GiB, of which 92% is the reconciler's .bridge_state cache containing bookkeeping fields (baseline_advanced_at, last_get_pass) that are never read, causing git delta compression to fail across scattered edits to the 18 MB bindings.json file.

Deleting the baseline_advanced_at timestamp and moving last_get_pass rotation bookkeeping to a separate file reduces the marginal packed cost per version from 12.79 KB to 1.74 KB (7.4x improvement) and halves version count churn, achieving ≤25% of baseline cost.

The reconciler runs on ephemeral GitHub-hosted runners, requiring durable .bridge_state state to remain in git; re-homing it off-branch was previously evaluated and rejected because the convergence loop self-heals binding drift through content and churn levers, not location.

A one-time history rewrite using git fast-export/fast-import removes only historical versions of target paths while preserving all 49,888 commits and 2,661 merges; the rewritten HEAD tree remains byte-identical to the pre-rewrite tip and reclaims ~1 GiB (1.17 GB → 98.8 MB).

The reclaim executes only after A1–A5 migrations (baseline field deletion, last_get_pass relocation, text normalization, prev_snapshot narrowing) close and A6 pre-flight checks (epoch guard deployment, review-bot convergence, off-repo backup verification) complete, with operator-attested quiescence confirmation and no active sessions or reconcile processes.

Post-reclaim rollback is an explicit quiesced window using --force-with-lease to restore the old ticket tip from an off-repo bundle, followed by mandatory reset and re-clone of all writers (shared tracker, review-bot EBS clone, ephemeral workflows) to re-establish epoch consistency before re-enabling writes.
